about: J-PCMCI+'s own published measurements, one file per lane; the release summary's J-PCMCI+ entries are built from it
build: Andrey pre-release build of 8 November 2026 (version string 0.15.0); refitted on the 0.15.0 release branch, Andrey's arm returned the same graph on all 1,760 fits of the linear cells
comparator: tigramite 5.2.10.1 JPCMCIplus, the implementation of J-PCMCI+ in the package of the method's authors, with the fix patches/tigramite-jpcmciplus-context-links.patch applied in memory
verdict_rule: per cell, level, and error: D = error(Andrey) - error(tigramite) per draw (one seed's datasets), on the draws both finished; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise; a row with fewer than 10 paired datasets is reported, not judged. 10,000 resamples of the draws, default_rng(0). The claim is judged at alpha 0.05, the paper's level, on the system SHD of every claimed cell and the context error where every context is observed; in a cell with a hidden context, the draws where a hidden context confounds an observed context and a system variable (Assumption 3 broken) form a row of their own, reported, not judged. Better or worse counts only if a rerun on fresh seeds agrees. An in-claim row also fails when an Andrey fit did not finish where tigramite's did. Floor: the floor applies only where tigramite's interval of its error minus the empty graph's lies wholly below 0, and there Andrey's must lie wholly below 0 too
fit_protocol: each fit in a fresh interpreter on one core with one BLAS thread, after one untimed warm-up fit (none with GPDC, nor for tigramite above 5 system variables, where a fit runs for minutes); a cap of 1,800 s and 16,000 MB per fit with imports and warm-up, past which a fit is a timeout, never an empty graph; each package's time runs from the datasets in memory to the returned graph, tigramite's including its dummies and DataFrame; each row's ratio is the median over the paired draws of tigramite's time over Andrey's, and its speed_ratio_median the median of Andrey's time over tigramite's
error_metric: shd: the endpoint SHD over the links between system variables at lags 0 to 2: a missing or extra link costs its two marks, a wrong mark one; for the entries named context links, the links from the observed contexts into the system variables that a fit misses plus those it adds. andrey_errors, comparator_errors, and empty_errors are medians over the paired draws, the _shd_mean fields their means, and andrey_adjacency_f1 and comparator_adjacency_f1 the mean F1 of the links between system variables, whatever their marks
seeds_note: seeds is the number of draws in the row, each one seed's datasets: every cell runs seeds 0-19, and the cells with a hidden context seeds 0-39, split into the draws where Assumption 3 holds and those where it breaks. No in-claim row came out better or worse, so no rerun ran
